name: bluewater-22-wrong-customer
lines: This customer paid every cent he owed. And the job still cost Bruno money.
Bruno installs kitchen cabinets. He's good. He's fair. And he says yes to everybody.
That last part is the problem.
There were four warning signs. He saw every one. Count them with me.
Sign one. The first phone call. The very first sentence.
What's the cheapest you can do it for?
Not, when can you start. Not, can I see your work. The cheapest.
Everybody asks about price. That's normal. But it was the only thing he asked.
Sign two. The last guy.
The last guy was useless, he says. And the one before him. And the one before that.
Three contractors. All terrible. What are the odds?
When everyone before you was the problem, guess who's next.
Sign three. The paperwork.
Bruno writes the quote. Twelve cabinets. And he says, just write kitchen. We'll figure it out as we go.
We'll figure it out means, I'll decide later what you owe me.
But Bruno wants the job. So he writes one word. Kitchen.
Sign four. The deposit.
Bruno asks for one. He says, I'll pay when it's done. Don't you trust me?
And Bruno, in a slow week, says, sure.
So the job starts. And here is what four ignored signs cost.
Day two. While you're here, can you move that outlet?
Day four. Actually, I want different handles. Can you swap them? All of them?
Day six. A text at eleven at night. Then six more.
A five day job takes eleven days.
He does pay. Thirty days late. After two reminders.
Now do the math Bruno didn't. Six extra days. Two jobs pushed back. And one of those hired somebody else.
He got paid in full. And he still came out behind.
Here's what Bruno finally worked out. This was not bad luck.
Look at his truck. Look at his ad. Cheapest in town. Free estimates. No job too small.
He wasn't unlucky. He was advertising for that exact customer.
Your marketing is a filter. It decides who calls, before you ever pick up.
So he changed three things.
One. The words. Cheapest came off the truck. Now it says, done right, in writing, on schedule.
People who only want cheap now have less reason to call. That's the point.
Two. The quote. Every quote lists exactly what's included. A change gets a price before it gets done.
Three. The deposit. Same for everyone. No deposit, no start date.
And he learned one sentence. I don't think I'm the right fit for this one.
It's the hardest sentence in business. He practised it in the truck.
Three weeks later, the phone rings. First sentence. What's the cheapest you can do it for?
Bruno smiles. I'm not the cheapest. Here's what I do. Still interested?
Sometimes they hang up. That's the filter working.
Sometimes they say, tell me more. That's a customer.
Not every customer is your customer. Marketing isn't about more calls. It's about the right ones.
Your business. Our marketing department. Bluewater Co.
